note: The jukebox catalogue. Every track here is 'verifiable': recovered through a published colour bar and carrying a contract, a tolerance and a live residual. The 'unanchored' tier still exists in tracks.js and is still enforced - a track may not claim to be verifiable without naming the bar it came from - but nothing unanchored ships. The visualizations that fall in that tier, and why, are named in the written legend instead: shipping them as entries that cannot be played made them look unfinished rather than deliberate.

tracks.label: Sea surface temperature
tracks.frameAlt: A global map of ocean surface currents drawn as fine flowing streamlines, coloured by water temperature: deep blue near both poles, green through the mid-latitudes, and a broad orange and red belt across the tropics. Continents are flat grey.
tracks.barSource: the 0–32 °C bar printed on the Perpetual Ocean frame
tracks.sourceLabel: SVS 3912 · Global Sea Surface Currents and Temperature
tracks.blurb: An ECCO2 still of global surface currents, listened to from the north pole to the south. The tropical belt is loud and the polar water is quiet, and that contrast is the ocean's heat, recovered from the picture's own colours.

terms.balanceLabel: the middle of the published 0–32 °C bar

tracks.label: Tropospheric NO₂
tracks.frameAlt: Nitrogen dioxide over the north-eastern United States, averaged over Marches from 2015 to 2019. Dark plumes sit over the cities of the eastern seaboard, brightest over New York, with lighter trails along the corridor toward Washington and over the Great Lakes.
tracks.barSource: the 0–10 ×10¹⁵ molecules/cm² NO₂ bar published with the frame
tracks.blurb: An air-quality still swept top to bottom. Its colour bar inverts almost exactly, so the numbers are firm — but only the plume pixels are data. The basemap underneath them is not, and it falls silent rather than reading as clean air.

terms.balanceLabel: the middle of the published 0–10 bar
